title: Changes sheet guide
course: CIS 110 LN182 · Introduction to Computers · Fall 2026, second 8-week session

intro.eyebrow: Capstone project · game version · the Changes sheet
paragraphs: The **Changes** sheet in `GameData.xlsx` is your team's record of what changed in your files and why. Your team keeps it from checkpoint 2 to the end.
Your files have no branches or merges like the version control programmers use. This sheet is how a teammate catches up on what changed while they were away.
intro.note: The Changes lead makes sure the sheet is complete at each checkpoint. Everyone adds rows for their own changes.

edition.print_note: This is the printable version of the Changes sheet guide. The web version is at `{site}`.

next.label: Next checkpoint
next.finished_text: Final submissions were due on {long:C7}. Watch Blackboard for your grade and feedback.

C1.summary: Join a team in Blackboard and introduce yourself in your team discussion.
C1.detail: Join a team in Blackboard. Then post a short introduction in your team discussion: when you can work, and what games you like. Use the team discussion to talk until your shared folder is ready.
todo: Join a team of {team_min} to {team_max} in Blackboard
Post an introduction in your team discussion
Reply to each teammate's introduction

C2.summary: Choose your game idea, give each person a role, and create your shared folder.
C2.detail: Each member pitches one game idea in the team discussion, and your team picks one. The Coordinator then creates the shared folder and shares it with everyone, including me. Each member declares a role by adding a row to the **Team** sheet. The Changes lead adds the first rows to the **Changes** sheet, and your team writes a short team charter.
todo: Pitch one game idea each in your team discussion
Choose one idea and a Coordinator as a team
Create the shared folder and add the three templates
Share the folder with every teammate and me as **Can edit**
Declare your role: add your row to the **Team** sheet
Changes lead: log your idea and roles in the **Changes** sheet

C3.summary: Have a draft of the design document in your folder.
C3.detail: Every heading in the design document has text. Each member leaves at least one comment on a section that someone else wrote.
todo: Write something under every heading in `GameDesign.docx`
Comment on one section a teammate wrote
Log this checkpoint's changes in the **Changes** sheet

C4.summary: Have a draft of the game data workbook in your folder.
C4.detail: The workbook has at least {min_rows} complete rows of game data, and every number in the design document appears in it.
todo: Fill at least {min_rows} complete rows in `GameData.xlsx`
Move every number from the design document into the workbook
Comment on one sheet a teammate filled
Log this checkpoint's changes in the **Changes** sheet

C5.summary: Have a draft of the presentation and its recording in your folder, so everything is in.
C5.detail: Every slide in the presentation has a draft, and one member has recorded a video presenting it, saved as `GamePitch.mp4`. After this deadline, I download your folder and build a playable prototype of your game over Thanksgiving break.
todo: Draft every slide in `GamePitch.pptx`
Draw a mock-up of one screen with shapes
Record one member presenting the slides, and save `GamePitch.mp4` in the folder
Comment on one slide a teammate made
Log this checkpoint's changes in the **Changes** sheet
C5.line: PowerPoint design summary and presentation recording in shared folder

C6.summary: Play your prototype and add your change requests.
C6.detail: From {links_by}, play the prototype I send you and add what should change to the **Changes** sheet. Each member adds at least one request by this date. You can keep adding requests until {long:C7}.
todo: Play your team's prototype
Add at least one change request each to the **Changes** sheet, with **Kind** set to **Request**
Read my replies and comments in your files

C7.summary: Submit your final files, the folder link, and each member's contribution.
C7.detail: Submit the folder link in Blackboard with one sentence about what each member contributed. Then complete the private peer rating survey in Blackboard. After this deadline, I plan to make a final pass on your game using your change requests.
todo: Make your final edits to all three files
Check that the **Changes** sheet is complete
Submit the folder link in Blackboard with each member's contribution
Complete the private peer rating survey

stats.label: Office files in one shared folder

status.break: No checkpoints. I build your games over the break.

sections.heading: What each column holds
lede: One row is one change. Keep the header row as it is, because I use it to read the sheet.

items.text: Number the rows 1, 2, 3, and so on. Don't reuse a number or delete a row.

items.title: Checkpoint
items.text: The checkpoint the change belongs to, from 2 to {checkpoints}.

items.title: Kind
items.text: **Change we made** for an edit to your files. **Request** for something you want changed in the prototype, after you play it.

items.title: Change, in your words
items.text: One sentence: what changed, or what you want. Write it so a teammate who missed the last week understands it.

items.title: Where in the files
items.text: The file and the heading or sheet, such as `GameDesign.docx`, section 4.

items.title: Why
items.text: The reason, in one sentence. For a request, say what happened when you played the prototype.

items.title: Added by (role)
items.text: Your role, such as Data lead. Use your role, not your name.

sections.heading: When to add rows
lede: The sheet is part of every checkpoint from 2 on.

items.title: Start the log
items.text: By {short:C2}, add the first rows: the idea your team chose and who holds each role.

items.title: Log each change
items.text: Whoever makes a change adds its row. Before each checkpoint, the Changes lead checks that nothing is missing.

items.title: Add requests
items.text: From {links_by}, play the prototype. Each member adds at least one row with **Kind** set to **Request** by {short:C6}.

items.title: Reply
items.text: I reply to each request in a comment on its row, until {short:C7}.

items.title: Final check
items.text: Before {short:C7}, read the sheet top to bottom. I use your requests for the final pass.

items.title: Log it
items.text: A new, changed, or removed rule, control, number, screen, or idea. A section moved from one file to another. A decision your team reversed.

items.title: Skip it
items.text: A typo fix, formatting, or rewording that keeps the meaning.

items.title: Not sure
items.text: Log it. A short row costs less than a teammate building on an old version.

sections.heading: Example rows
lede: These rows come from the example folder for Lava Lanes, a made-up game on the assignment page.

items.title: Row 1 · checkpoint 2 · Change we made
items.text: We chose Lava Lanes and recorded each person's role in the **Team** sheet. Added by: Changes lead.

items.title: Row 2 · checkpoint 3 · Change we made
items.text: Ember starts with 3 hearts, not 5. Where: `GameDesign.docx`, section 4. Why: with five hearts we never lost in our paper test. Added by: Design writer.

items.title: Row 3 · checkpoint 4 · Change we made
items.text: We put every rule in the **Rules** sheet, each with a worked example. Where: **Rules** sheet and section 4. Why: the template asks for the full list in the **Rules** sheet. Added by: Data lead.

items.title: Row 4 · checkpoint 6 · Request
items.text: Ember moves too slowly between lanes. Where: **Things** sheet, Ember's speed. Why: rocks hit us before we can move. Added by: Presenter.

items.title: Do I add rows, or only the Changes lead?
items.text: Everyone adds rows for their own changes. The Changes lead makes sure the sheet is complete at each checkpoint.

items.title: Version history already shows changes. Why keep this sheet?
items.text: Version history shows who changed a file and when. It doesn't say what the change means or why, and your teammates need both.

items.title: Is the sheet graded?
items.text: It's part of shared-folder organization and collaboration. I check it at each checkpoint and read it when I grade your folder.

items.title: We changed our minds. Can we delete a row?
items.text: No. Add a new row that says what changed back, and why.
